page_title: You Can Increase Your Intelligence: 5 Ways to Maximize Your Cognitive Potential

sources.entry: You can increase your intelligence: 5 ways to maximize your cognitive potential: forgive the clickbait title, it’s actually a good article.

summary.title: You Can Increase Your Intelligence: 5 Ways to Maximize Your Cognitive Potential
summary.one_liner: Learn the author's five everyday principles for boosting fluid intelligence (seek novelty, challenge yourself, think creatively, do things the hard way, network), grounded in working-memory training research.
takeaways: Fluid intelligence, the capacity to learn and retain new information, is presented as trainable, with gains that depend on the amount of training.
Brain-training games like Sudoku improve performance on those games but are argued not to raise general intelligence; moving on to new challenges is recommended.
Efficiency can reduce cognitive growth: the Tetris study showed brain activity dropping once the skill was mastered, so keep taking on harder tasks.
Everyday habits suggested include learning new skills, creative thinking, avoiding over-reliance on GPS and autocorrect, and networking with diverse people.
summary.summary: This guest blog post, originally on Scientific American's former blog network, argues that fluid intelligence can be improved. It starts with the author's experience as a behavior therapist and the 2008 Jaeggi et al. study on dual n-back working memory training, then summarizes related studies on dopamine, plasticity, Tetris training, and Sternberg's Rainbow Project. The author turns these findings into five practical principles for daily life, each supported by references to research, and many claims are the author's own opinion rather than the cited data.
